title: Analysis of proteins by a radical-free and highly reducing method of two-dimensional polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis
author: Wada, Akira
materials: As shown in Figure 1, RFHR 2-D PAGE consists of three polyacrylamide gels. All gels are infused with 2-aminoethanethiol HCl, a radical scavenger and reducing agent, prior to protein electrophoresis (prerun). This removes free radicals and transforms the oxidizing gel environment into a strongly reducing one. Cysteine residues in proteins are maintained in a reduced state throughout electrophoresis by 2-aminoethanethiol HCl, and noise caused by cysteine dimerization is eliminated thoroughly. Therefore, one type of protein converges on a single spot. Prior to the first-dimensional electrophoresis, sample charging (SC) electrophoresis is performed to concentrate the protein sample using a leading ion and trailing ion. A sample gel fragment less than 1 cm in size containing the concentrated proteins is embedded into the one-dimensional gel. In the first-dimensional electrophoresis, proteins migrate mainly based on their charge magnitude: positively charged proteins move to the right and negatively charged proteins move to the left at pH 8.3. After the first-dimensional gel is laid atop the second-dimensional gel, the second-dimensional electrophoresis is performed at pH 3.6. Proteins migrate from top to bottom mainly based on their molecular size. Very small basic proteins also form normal spots. The completed two-dimensional gel is typically stained with Coomassie brilliant blue (CBB) G250 and destained. Protein spots on the two-dimensional gel are measured using a GS800 calibrated densitometer (Bio-Rad 232 Laboratories Inc., Hercules, CA, United States).

Gel solutions and electrode buffers were prepared each time, using stocked concentrated buffers as follows. Sample charging (SC) buffer (50×): 24 mL 5 N KOH, 74 mL glacial acetic acid, and water in 200 mL; 1-D buffer (4×): 32.0 g EDTA-2Na (Dojindo Kumamoto Japan, Guaranteed Reagent (GR)), 128 g boric acid, 194.5 g Tris, and water in 1 L; 2-D gel buffer (10×): 96 mL 5 N KOH, 523 mL glacial acetic acid and water in 1 L; 2-D electrode buffer (10×): 16.0 mL glacial acetic acid, 150 g glycine (FUJIFILM Wako GR), and water in 1 L.

The stained 2-D gel patterns were scanned using a GS800 calibrated densitometer (Bio-Rad Laboratories Inc., Hercules, CA, United States). The optical density (OD)/molecular weight (MW) of each r-protein was calculated. Among them, the values of the ten proteins (S4, S5, S7, S13, L18, L22, L24, L25, L27, and L29) were designated as unit copy proteins (Hardy, 1975; Tal et al., 1990). The average of these OD/MW values was set to 1, and the copy number of each protein was expressed as a ratio relative to the unit copy proteins. The OD/MW values of each r-protein and ribosome-binding factor were converted to copy numbers.

steps.title: Grow and store E. coli cultures
steps.instruction: Grow E. coli K12 W3110 wild‑type and W3110 ΔompT::Km in medium E supplemented with 2 % (w/v) hipolypeptone and 0.5 % (w/v) glucose at 37 °C; harvest cells at log or stationary phase and store pellets at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare crude ribosomes (CR)
steps.instruction: Grind frozen cell pellets with an equal volume of quartz sand, extract with buffer I (20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.6, 15 mM Mg‑acetate, 100 mM NH₄OAc, 6 mM 2‑mercaptoethanol), centrifuge 9 000 × g 15 min 4 °C, keep supernatant (CE) and resuspend pellet in buffer I; repeat centrifugation, collect the second pellet as cell‑debris (CD). Layer the combined CE onto a 30 % (w/v) sucrose cushion in buffer I and centrifuge in a Beckman 55.2 Ti rotor at 206 000 × g for 3 h at 4 °C. Resuspend the resulting pellet in buffer I as crude ribosomes (CR) and keep the supernatant as post‑ribosomal supernatant (PRS).

steps.title: Prepare high‑salt‑washed ribosome (HSR)
steps.instruction: Resuspend CR in buffer II (20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.6, 10 mM Mg‑acetate, 1 M NH₄OAc, 6 mM 2‑mercaptoethanol) and mix 1 h at 4 °C. Layer 20 mL of this suspension onto a 30 % (w/v) sucrose cushion in buffer II (10 mL) and centrifuge in the same rotor at 206 000 × g for 4 h at 4 °C. Resuspend the pellet in buffer I and dialyze overnight against buffer I. The resulting suspension is the HSR.

steps.title: Prepare ribosome sucrose gradients
steps.instruction: Layer each ribosome sample (CR, HSR, PRS, or CD) onto a 5 %–20 % (w/v) sucrose density gradient (SDG) prepared in buffer I, then centrifuge in a Beckman SW 40 Ti rotor at 25 000 × g for 20 h at 4 °C. Measure absorbance of each fraction at 260 nm with a Shimadzu UV‑1800 spectrometer.

steps.title: Prepare proteins by acetic‑acid method
steps.instruction: Dialyze each fraction (CR, PRS, CD) against 2 % (v/v) acetic acid three times, lyophilize the dialysate with a Labconco freeze‑dryer, and store the dried proteins at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare stock buffers
steps.instruction: Make the following 50× or 10× stock solutions:

substeps.instruction: SC buffer (50×): 24 mL 5 N KOH, 74 mL glacial acetic acid, add water to 200 mL.
1‑D buffer (4×): 32.0 g EDTA‑2Na, 128 g boric acid, 194.5 g Tris, add water to 1 L.
2‑D gel buffer (10×): 96 mL 5 N KOH, 523 mL glacial acetic acid, add water to 1 L.
2‑D electrode buffer (10×): 16.0 mL glacial acetic acid, 150 g glycine, add water to 1 L.

steps.title: Prepare SC gel solution and buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare SC gel solution and its prerun/run buffers as follows:

substeps.instruction: SC gel (100 mL): 42.0 g urea, 7.0 g acrylamide, 0.125 g bisacrylamide, 0.3 mL TEMED, 2 mL SC buffer (50×), add water to 100 mL; add 1/100 volume of 10 % (w/v) ammonium persulfate just before casting.
Anode prerun buffer (100 mL): 45.0 g urea, 1.0 g 2‑aminoethanethiol HCl, 2 mL SC buffer (50×), add water to 100 mL.
Cathode prerun buffer (100 mL): same as anode prerun buffer but omit 2‑aminoethanethiol HCl.
Anode run buffer (100 mL): 24.0 g urea, 3.5 g cysteine‑HCl, 10 mL 2‑D electrode buffer (10×), add water to 100 mL.
Cathode run buffer (100 mL): 36.0 g urea, 10 mL 2‑D gel buffer (10×), add water to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 1‑D gel solution and buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare the 1‑D gel solution and its prerun/run buffers:

substeps.instruction: 1‑D gel (100 mL): 42.0 g urea, 7.0 g acrylamide, 0.125 g bisacrylamide, 0.3 mL TEMED, 25 mL 1‑D buffer (4×), add water to 100 mL; add 1/100 volume of 10 % (w/v) ammonium persulfate before casting.
Anode prerun/run buffer (100 mL): 45.0 g urea, 1.0 g 2‑aminoethanethiol HCl, 25 mL 1‑D buffer (4×), add water to 100 mL.
Cathode prerun/run buffer (100 mL): same as anode buffer but without 2‑aminoethanethiol HCl.

steps.title: Prepare 2‑D gel solution and buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare the 2‑D gel solution and its prerun/run buffers:

substeps.instruction: 2‑D gel (1 L): 420 g urea, 170 g acrylamide, 4.7 g bisacrylamide, 5.8 mL TEMED, 100 mL 2‑D gel buffer (10×), add water to 1 L; add 1/30 volume of 10 % ammonium persulfate before casting.
Anode prerun buffer (400 mL): 168 g urea, 2.0 g 2‑aminoethanethiol HCl, 40 mL 2‑D gel buffer (10×), add water to 400 mL.
Cathode prerun buffer (400 mL): 40 mL 2‑D gel buffer (10×), add water to 400 mL.
Anode run buffer (400 mL): 168 g urea, 14 g cysteine‑HCl, 40 mL 2‑D electrode buffer (10×), add water to 400 mL.
Cathode run buffer (400 mL): 1.0 mL concentrated HCl (35‑37 %), 40 mL 2‑D electrode buffer (10×), add water to 400 mL.

steps.title: Prepare ribosomal protein sample
steps.instruction: Dissolve lyophilized ribosomal protein mixture in 40‑fold‑diluted 1‑D buffer (4×) containing 8 M urea and 0.2 M 2‑mercaptoethanol; incubate 40 °C for 30 min, then add 1/25 volume of SC buffer (50×). Add pyronine‑G and, if desired, recrystallized acridine orange as migration markers. Load 0.3–1.0 mg (20 mg mL⁻¹) of ribosomal proteins onto the gel; treat CD and PRS fractions identically.

steps.title: Run sample‑charging (SC) electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Cast SC gel in a short gel container (six chambers, 60 mm height, 2 × 5 mm² cross‑section) up to 40 mm height, overlay with water and gelate. Perform a prerun at 100 V for 1 h using the SC prerun buffers. After prerun, add each protein sample to its respective gel chamber, gently overlay with anode run buffer, and run at 100 V for 10–30 min until pyronine‑G and acridine orange have migrated ~10 mm. Loosen the gels, inject SC anode run buffer through a needle to release the gels, and cut gel pieces immediately below the marker band, each ≤10 mm long. Collect these sample gel pieces for the subsequent 1‑D electrophoresis.

steps.title: Assemble and run 1‑D electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Assemble the 1‑D apparatus (open gel container with six chambers, 175 mm height, 2 × 5 mm² cross‑section) and seal it to the anode buffer vessel using 1‑D gel solution. Gelate the bottom of each chamber, then fill the chambers with 1‑D gel solution and gelate. Perform a prerun at 100 V for 3 h. Open the sample‑gel cover, cut the exposed gel to match the length of the SC gel pieces, insert each sample gel piece, add a small amount of 1‑D anode run buffer to eliminate bubbles, and reseal the cover. Run the 1‑D electrophoresis at 100 V for ~24 h at room temperature with air cooling. After the run, remove the 1‑D gel and the embedded sample gel pieces, trim excess gel to the width of the forthcoming 2‑D gel, and note that the cathode‑side gel length should be twice the anode‑side length.

steps.title: Assemble and run 2‑D electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Assemble the 2‑D gel container (left part, three middle parts, right part) using four hataganes; insert it into the anode buffer vessel and place on a 2‑D gel dish. Add 30 mL of 2‑D gel solution to the dish and gelate to form the bottom layer. Seal the interfaces, then fill the gel chambers and side grooves with 2‑D gel solution. Insert 1‑D gel spacers to create 5 mm deep slots for the 1‑D and sample gels, gelate, then remove spacers and excess gel. Perform a prerun at 100 V for 24 h with air cooling. Place the completed 1‑D gel and the sample gel pieces onto the solidified 2‑D gel, avoiding bubbles. Cover the assembly with a piece of fine cotton gauze or nylon stocking wetted with anode run buffer, and press firmly with five pressing wedges inserted into the grooves. Run the 2‑D electrophoresis at 100 V for ~24 h at room temperature with air cooling, using the pyronine‑G front marker from the 1‑D gel; stop when the marker reaches the bottom of the gel.

steps.title: Stain and destain 2‑D gels
steps.instruction: Remove the 2‑D gels from the chamber, stain them in 0.25 % (w/v) Coomassie Brilliant Blue G 250 prepared in 9 % (v/v) acetic acid for 30 min. Destain by shaking in 3 % (v/v) acetic acid + 30 % (v/v) ethanol, then repeat destaining in 2 % (v/v) acetic acid until the background is clear.

steps.title: Scan gels and calculate copy numbers
steps.instruction: Scan the stained 2‑D gels with a Bio‑Rad GS800 calibrated densitometer. Compute optical density (OD) per molecular weight (MW) for each ribosomal protein; set the average OD/MW of the ten reference proteins (S4, S5, S7, S13, L18, L22, L24, L25, L27, L29) to 1. Express each protein’s copy number as the ratio of its OD/MW to this unit value.

steps.title: Excise gel spot for mass spectrometry
steps.instruction: Punch out individual protein spots from the scanned 2‑D gel, place each spot into a microtube, and send to a contractor for protein identification by mass spectrometry.
